paragraphs: Baker, here's the big idea. Hearing the word is only the start. James says, "Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves." (James 1:22) You can sit through the whole thing, nod, take notes, and still walk out the same as you walked in.

That's why James starts with listening. He says everyone should be "quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger," because "man's anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires." (James 1:19-20) So the humble listening comes first, and then comes the doing. He also says the one who keeps looking into "the perfect law of freedom" and keeps at it "will be blessed in what he does." (James 1:25) The blessing is in the doing, friend, and I'm not saying that with flour on my face. Okay, I AM, but I'm still right.

And the doing is real, everyday stuff. A tongue with no bridle makes religion worthless, but pure religion cares for "orphans and widows in their distress" and keeps you from being polluted by the world. (James 1:26-27) So here's your batch for today, baker: pick one thing you heard, and do it before the dough gets cold. The word planted in you can save your soul, and it's meant to get out of the bowl and into the oven. (James 1:21)
